title: IARPA request to study CRISPR-Cas9 DNA data encoding

tellings.quote: the current deputy director dni Stacy Dixon was the director when I was asked could I take a look at using CRA crisper cast 9 encoding information into DNA

plain: Bob Maguire, a contractor who worked for the CIA, says that around 2013 or 2014 he was asked to look into storing information inside DNA. The method was CRISPR-Cas9, a tool for editing genes. He says the request came from IARPA, the US intelligence agencies' research funding office, while he was at the Hume Center, a research center at Virginia Tech. He adds that IARPA was then run by Stacy Dixon, who later became deputy director of national intelligence, the second-highest official over US spy agencies.
